title: Model homotopy colimit cocones become localized colimits
statement:
Use simplicial sets and infinity categories in fixed universes [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A combinatorial model category $\mathcal M$ means a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category with weak equivalences $W$ closed under retracts and satisfying two-out-of-three, and classes of cofibrations $C$ and fibrations $F$ such that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems generated by sets, with functorial factorizations. Locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A weak factorization system is a factorization of every arrow into its left and right classes, each class characterized by diagonal lifting against the other. A cofibrant object has its initial map in $C$. There exists a universal homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$: restriction into any infinity category identifies the functor infinity category out of the target with the full subcategory of functors out of $N(\mathcal M)$ inverting $W$.

For every small ordinary category $I$, the projective model structure on $\mathcal M^I$ exists, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. If $D:I\to\mathcal M$ and $QD\to D$ is a projectively cofibrant replacement, then the ordinary colimit cocone $QD\to\operatorname{colim}_I QD$, after applying $q$ and identifying $qQD$ with $qD$, is a colimit cocone in $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$. In particular a model homotopy pushout square, meaning a cocone on a span for which the comparison from the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement is a weak equivalence, becomes a pushout square there. This assertion includes the maps of the cocone and its coherent universal property, and does not assume that $\mathcal M$ is simplicial or that the original diagram $D$ is objectwise cofibrant.

source.place: Section 2.3, projective diagram model structures and Example 2.3.21; Section 7.9, Theorem 7.9.8 and Remark 7.9.10, with the dual colimit statements. No Stacks tag states this coherent-localization comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] to the nerve of $\mathcal M$ with system $W$. Identities and composition belong to $W$ by the model axioms; in an ordinary nerve closure under homotopy is automatic. This gives $q:N\mathcal M\to\mathcal C$ with precisely the functor-category universal property in the statement. The same construction applies to any ordinary diagram category with objectwise weak equivalences. All categories and Hom sets are taken in a fixed larger universe while the indexing category and coproducts remain $\mathcal U$-small. The functor $q$ is essentially surjective. Indeed let $\mathcal C'$ be the full subcategory on objects equivalent to some $qX$. Its factorization $q':N\mathcal M\to\mathcal C'$ inverts $W$, so the universal property extends it to $r:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$. For the inclusion $j:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal C$, full faithfulness of restriction gives $jr\simeq1_{\mathcal C}$ from $jrq\simeq q$; hence every object lies in $\mathcal C'$ up to equivalence.

source.place: Section 7.1, localization universal property; Section 7.9, fixed universe convention.

proof.text: Construct limits and colimits of $I$-diagrams pointwise: the map at an arrow of $I$ is the unique map induced by the corresponding family of maps on the limiting or colimiting components. The component universal properties give the universal property for natural transformations, so $\mathcal A=\mathcal M^I$ is complete and cocomplete. For $i\in I$ define $E_i(A)_j=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}A$, with an arrow $j\to k$ sending the summand $\alpha$ to its composite summand. A natural map $E_i(A)\to D$ is determined by $A\to D_i$ on the identity summand, its $\alpha$-component being the composite with $D(\alpha)$. Thus $E_i\dashv\operatorname{ev}_i$. Let $K,J$ be the given sets generating respectively the cofibration/trivial-fibration and trivial-cofibration/fibration weak factorization systems of $\mathcal M$. Put $K_I=\{E_i k\}$ and $J_I=\{E_i j\}$. Lifting squares under this explicit adjunction show that $K_I^{\square}$ consists exactly of objectwise trivial fibrations and $J_I^{\square}$ of objectwise fibrations.

source.place: Section 2.3.10, projective classes; explicit free-evaluation adjunction and pointwise universal properties.

proof.text: For every domain $A$ of a map of $K$ or $J$, [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] supplies an infinite regular presentability cardinal $\tau_A$. Bound the small family of these cardinals by one infinite regular $\lambda>\tau_A$ using [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound], applied to the disjoint union of sets of cardinalities $\tau_A$. A continuous $\lambda$-chain is $\tau_A$-filtered: any fewer than $\tau_A$ stages have an upper bound below $\lambda$ by regularity. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E_iA,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A,\operatorname{ev}_i(-))$ preserves its colimit, since evaluation computes colimits pointwise. Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] separately to $K_I$ and $J_I$. It gives functorial factorizations into a relative cell map and a map in the respective right lifting class, and identifies each left lifting class with retracts of the corresponding relative cell maps. This checks smallness in $\mathcal A$ directly; no unproved assertion that a functor category is locally presentable is needed.

source.place: Section 2.4, small object argument; projective generation expanded with the cited cardinal-smallness statements.

proof.text: Write $L_K={}^{\square}(K_I^{\square})$, $L_J={}^{\square}(J_I^{\square})$. The factorizations and retract characterization in [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] give the two weak factorization systems $(L_K,K_I^{\square})$ and $(L_J,J_I^{\square})$. At each object, an $E_i(j)$ is a coproduct of copies of the trivial cofibration $j$. Coproducts, pushouts and continuous transfinite compositions of maps left orthogonal to fibrations remain left orthogonal to fibrations: choose the lift on each coproduct summand, extend a lift across each successor pushout, and take its uniquely induced map at a limit stage. Retracts preserve lifts by composing a lift with the retract maps. Hence evaluating a $J_I$-cell map, or its retract, gives a trivial cofibration in $\mathcal M$. Consequently $L_J\subset W_I$; also $L_J\subset L_K$ since objectwise trivial fibrations are objectwise fibrations. Conversely, if $a\in L_K\cap W_I$, factor $a=pj$ with $j\in L_J$ and $p$ an objectwise fibration. Two-out-of-three gives $p\in W_I$, so $p\in K_I^{\square}$. A lift in the square with left map $a$, right map $p$, top map $j$ and bottom identity exhibits $a$ as an arrow retract of $j$. Thus $a\in L_J$. We have proved $L_J=L_K\cap W_I$. Since $W_I$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three componentwise, these two functorial weak factorization systems are exactly the required projective model structure. This includes $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Section 2.3.10 and Section 2.4; direct verification of projective model axioms from the cellular factorizations.

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{colim}_I:\mathcal A\to\mathcal M$ and $G=\Delta_I$. Their adjunction sends $h:FD\to Y$ to the cocone with components $h\iota_i$. The right adjoint $G$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations because projective right classes are objectwise; equivalently, the explicit adjunction on lifting squares shows that $F$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant diagrams as follows. For such a weak equivalence $a$, [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $a=pi$ with $i,s$ cofibrations, $p$ a trivial fibration and $ps=1$. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Therefore $Fi,Fs$ are weak equivalences; $Fp\,Fs=1$ gives $Fp$ a weak equivalence, and so $Fa=Fp\,Fi$ is a weak equivalence. Notice that $G$ preserves all weak equivalences, not just those with fibrant endpoints.

source.place: Paragraph 2.3.14 and the Brown factorization argument of Section 2.3.

proof.text:
Choose a functorial projective cofibrant replacement $p:Q\to1_{\mathcal A}$ with each $p_D$ a trivial fibration. Naturality and two-out-of-three imply that $Q$ preserves $W_I$. Write $\mathcal A_c$ for the full cofibrant subcategory. Its inclusion $i$ and $Q:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_c$ are relative functors; $iQ\xrightarrow{p}1_{\mathcal A}$ and $Qi\xrightarrow{p}1_{\mathcal A_c}$ have weak-equivalence components. By the full functor-category assertion of [lem-coef-system-localization-universal], these functors and transformations localize. Componentwise equivalence detection from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the localized transformations equivalences, so $\mathcal A_c[W_I^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal A[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$. The relative functor $F|_{\mathcal A_c}$ of step 5 therefore defines $H$ on the latter localization, with $H(D)=qFQD$; $G$ localizes directly. Let $u:1\to GF$ and $v:FG\to1$ be the ordinary unit and counit. Localizing their indicated restrictions defines coherent natural transformations
$$\eta_D=u_{QD}\,p_D^{-1}:D\longrightarrow GH(D),\qquad \epsilon_Y=v_Y\,F(p_{GY}):HG(Y)\longrightarrow Y.$$
These are transformations between relative functors before the inverses of $p$ are inserted; restriction along localization is fully faithful on their entire functor categories, so their naturality diagrams descend as well.

source.place: Sections 7.1 and 7.5.25, explicit left replacement construction; agent expansion of the unit and counit.

proof.text:
Verify the two triangles and their effect on mapping spaces rather than invoking the existing model-derived-adjunction node. Naturality of $u$ and $vG\circ Gu=1_G$ give
$$G\epsilon_Y\,\eta_{GY}=Gv_Y\,GF(p_{GY})\,u_{QGY}\,p_{GY}^{-1}=Gv_Y\,u_{GY}=1.$$
The other composite simplifies, using naturality of $p$ at $u_{QD}$ and $vF\circ Fu=1_F$, to
$$\epsilon_{HD}\,H\eta_D=F(p_{QD})\,F(Qp_D)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $p$ at $p_D$ gives $p_Dp_{QD}=p_DQp_D$. Cancel the equivalence $p_D$ in $\mathcal A[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$. Both remaining arrows are between cofibrant diagrams; the fully faithful localized inclusion from step 6 identifies them also in $\mathcal A_c[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$. Applying the localized $F|_{\mathcal A_c}$ shows that the last display is $1$. All cancellations here are homotopies of the displayed natural transformations. Thus for arbitrary localized $D,Y$, the maps of spaces
$$h\longmapsto G(h)\eta_D,\qquad a\longmapsto\epsilon_Y H(a)$$
are mutual homotopy inverses: naturality rewrites their composites as $G\epsilon_Y\,\eta_{GY}\,a$ and $h\,\epsilon_{HD}\,H\eta_D$. This proves a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(qFQD,qY)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A[W_I^{-1}]_\infty}(D,GY)$, with the forward map induced by the specified replacement cocone. It is a mapping-space equivalence, not merely a bijection on components.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.30, elementary unit/counit computation spelling out its specialization without citing a cyclic DAG dependency.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] to $\mathcal M$ and $I$. It identifies $\mathcal A[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal C)$, its object $D$ with $qD$, and $GY$ with $\Delta_{N(I)}qY$, including transformations. The forward mapping-space equivalence of step 7 is therefore postcomposition of the localized colimit cocone with a map $qFQD\to qY$, after the identification $qQD\simeq qD$. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says exactly that this cocone is colimiting. The test includes every object of $\mathcal C$ by the essential-surjectivity argument in step 1. For completeness, given any specified projectively cofibrant replacement $e:E\to D$, lift $e$ against the trivial fibration $p_D:QD\to D$, obtaining $b:E\to QD$ over $D$. Two-out-of-three makes $b$ a weak equivalence between cofibrant diagrams. Step 5 makes $Fb$ a weak equivalence, and the two cocones commute with $b$ and $Fb$ by the ordinary colimit universal property. Their images are consequently equivalent cocones, so the conclusion holds for the specified replacement, not only for the functorially chosen one.

source.place: Theorem 7.9.8 and Remark 7.9.10, dual colimit interpretation, including the cocone maps.

proof.text: For a span diagram $D$, a model homotopy pushout cocone $D\to\Delta P$ has, by hypothesis, a weak equivalence $c:FE\to P$ from the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement. Its localized cocone is obtained from the colimiting cocone of step 8 by the equivalence $q(c)$ on the apex and the replacement equivalence on the boundary. For any $Y$, precomposition with $q(c)$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces, so the same cocone mapping-space criterion proves that this is a pushout. The argument uses projective cofibrancy of the replacement only; neither simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$ nor objectwise cofibrancy of $D$ has been introduced.

source.place: Example 2.3.21 and Definition 2.3.22; mapping-space cocone criterion.
